messages:
maya: seeing a KV cache OOM in hosted for a long-chat session. spill started but slab allocator didn't free enough and eviction didn't hand off quickly. attaching short profile dump and logs.

maya: log snippet: 
```
[info] kv: page_write 0x7f8... len=32MB
[warn] kv: slab_alloc failed returns ENOMEM
[debug] kv: eviction_scan took 1.2s, reclaimed 4MB
[error] runtime: OOM during generate -> abort
```

devon: ouch. is this the same flow where concurrent reads prevent evict from acquiring shard locks?

li: probably. I saw a repro where long ctx growth keeps pins on prefixes so the evictable set is tiny. eviction_scan is scanning but can't free because reuse refcounts >0.

sam: can you paste the profiler output? curious about kernel selection interplay (we've seen kernel switch add temp allocations).

maya: small profile attached inline: 
- peak resident: 58GB, baseline runtime process 12GB
- kv pages allocated: 45GB (mostly large slabs)
- hot paths: kv::write_lock, kernel::matmul_temp_alloc, kv::mark_reuse

maya: also noticed when kernel switches from fast-fp16 to emu-quant paths we allocate extra buffers for reorder, those are transient but overlap with eviction window.

devon: two thoughts: 1) introduce a soft-priority evict path that can steal from pinned entries with LRU grace if memory pressure exceeds X; 2) throttle kernel path that triggers heavy temp allocations while eviction in progress.

li: we should be careful: stealing pinned entries can break long-convo correctness. maybe prefer spill-to-disk fallback first (slow but correct), and only as last resort evict re-use entries with a version tombstone so future accesses can detect reload.

sam: agree. spilling currently is async and stalls on IO queue; also we have a reentrancy bug where page_reclaim callback tries to allocate a buffer and deadlocks. that explains the small reclaimed amount.

maya: repro steps I ran: start hosted with long-chat generator, set seq len ~65k, no prefix cache pinning; feed repeated personas -> growth. I toggled fallback quant kernel and saw slightly different timings but same OOM.

devon: quick mitigation can be: 1) add backoff to generation when eviction latency > 500ms (graceful degrade), 2) circuit-breaker to return 503+retry-after for new requests that would touch hot long contexts, 3) increase IO spill workers to drain faster.

li: operationally, we can add a metric kv.evict.latency and kv.spill.queue_len and alert when evict.latency > 1s. Also add a canary rollout of a fast path that drops oldest non-pinned prefix with a tombstone marker.

sam: for the deadlock in reclaim callback, patch incoming: avoid any allocation path in reclaim; use stack buffers and pre-allocated buffers from a per-thread pool. PR incoming.

maya: I'm going to attach the small reproducer script and run with patch of no-kernel-switch to see difference.

devon: plan of action: (1) hotfix reclaim callback to remove allocations (sam) (2) temporary throttle generator on hosted that hits long contexts (maya) (3) increase spill workers and add metric (li) (4) design graceful evict-with-tombstone and rollout behind feature flag (devon)

maya: assigning owners: sam -> reclaim patch, target deploy in next 2 hours; maya -> throttle + canary route config; li -> metrics + extra workers; devon -> design doc for tombstone eviction.

runtime-bot: deploy job started for sam/reclaim-patch (build 4122). status: running tests.

sam: tests passed locally, running integration in staging. found one flake in allocator that I'll fix quickly.

maya: thanks. after deploy we'll monitor kv.evict.latency and host oom alerts. I'll also add a temporary routing rule to route suspect sessions to dedicated pool to limit blast radius.

li: I'll instrument spill latency percentiles and add a dashboard.

devon: folks, long-term we should tie kernel selection heuristics to current memory pressure: prefer kernels with lower transient allocs under high pressure. adding that to perf backlog.

maya: agreed. ok closing this thread once reclaim patch is live and metrics show <200ms evict latency for 1hr. :thumbsup:

sam: reclaim patch live in staging. will prod tomorrow morning in prod window if green.

runtime-bot: deploy job succeeded for sam/reclaim-patch (build 4122).

maya: deployed to prod small cohort. initial telemetry: kv.evict.latency median 180ms, spill.queue_len down from 25->6. will continue monitoring.

devon: nice. keep an eye for any correctness regressions from tombstone idea later.

maya: closing for now, will reopen if we see recurrences. thanks all.
